assign.request: our new ai dashboard system still sucks... i never have a nice clean report of what happened. Build a fourth 'days' view on /framework/ai/v/3/ that reads only each task's landing line, newest day first, and make it the default view of /framework/ai/.
assign.now: reading page.js, timeline.js and the day/task log shapes
steps: read page.js's view switch and timeline.js, and the day.jsonl / task.jsonl data shapes
decide day.jsonl vs task.jsonl for the row list and write the decision
build the days view: day headings, landed rows folding to full outcome + links, quiet working lines for today
make days the default view, keep ?view= and saved now/grid prefs working
layout pass at 400/1280/1920 and css reuse check
reload hold, headless proof at three widths, screenshot, row-count check for today

log.msg: usage refresh skipped - fence names only v/3/** and this task dir, not ai/usage.json or ai/usage.jsonl, per the new-task skill's own caveat

read finish-task's own skill to see exactly how day.jsonl's landed line is written: a hand-picked one-line summary the minion writes itself at landing, separate from task.jsonl's own assign.outcome - not a machine-derived copy of it

counted task dirs under ai/: about 700 across 32 days (2026-08-12 through today), 693 landed lines total in day.jsonl files - fetching every landed task's own task.jsonl up front is 700 requests, not viable for a page load

decision.msg: Data source for the days list: ai/<date>/day.jsonl for the list and each row's headline, a task's own task.jsonl fetched lazily ONLY when that row's <details> is opened (via TaskJSONL from ext/JSONL/JSONL.js), never every landed task's task.jsonl up front. Alternative considered and rejected: fetch every landed task's task.jsonl eagerly (ext/AITask/dashboard.js's own all_tasks() already does exactly this, and reusing it would have cut a lot of new code) - rejected because there are about 700 task dirs across 32 days; that is 700 small requests on every page load just to read a headline, against 32 day.jsonl fetches this way. The day.jsonl 'landed - <one line>' message IS already a headline a task wrote for itself at landing time (finish-task skill step 4, a distinct hand-written line, not a machine copy of assign.outcome), so it stands in directly for 'the task's headline' the brief asks for; opening a row's fold is what actually reads assign.outcome (rendered as markdown, so its own bold headline shows there too) plus links and the task page link. Rule: code#8 (try to keep a file's own cost down; reuse what already exists) weighed against the new-task-log's own count of ~700 dirs.

Day list comes from Socket.singleton().ls('/framework/ai/') - the same dev-socket call this file's own ways_out() and open_mastermind_run() already use for the exact same date-dir listing - not directory.json (which ext/AITask/dashboard.js reads instead: a real, tested alternative, but a 1.9MB fetch for a list Socket.ls already gives this file cheaply, and this file has never read directory.json). Rule: css/code 'climb the ladder' - reuse this file's own established pattern before reaching for a different one that also works.

Today's unlanded tasks ('working - <now>'): <now> is the task's own live status text (assign.now, or the running agent still missing an outcome) via ext/AITask/card.js's current() and stats.js's state(), imported read-only - not reimplemented, and not the day.jsonl 'task opened' line's own wording, which never updates once written. Bounded to a handful of concurrent tasks on today's date only, so one small task.jsonl fetch per open task is cheap and always fresh, unlike the bulk-fetch rejected above for landed rows.

layout Q1-Q5: container is .v3-wall, the same box now/grid/timeline already render into (view-switched by page.js, no new page region) - Q4 stays at the two-or-three regions the page already has. Q2: one column, full width of .v3-wall, padded like .v3-cards/.v3-now already are (extending that existing rule to include .v3-days rather than writing a new padding rule). Q3: .flow for the day-to-day rhythm (page-level rhythm between date headings, which is exactly what .flow is for) and flex v gap-25 for the rows inside one day (a UI stack, not prose) - never both in one box, per the layout skill's own rhythm rule. Q5: no preview - this is the default top-level view, not a child page.

CSS: read v3.css in full before writing anything. Four new declarations only, all v3- prefixed (already an open namespace, checked against css-scopes.txt and a repo-wide grep for collisions - none): .v3-days added to the existing '.v3-cards, .v3-now { padding: var(--pad) }' rule instead of a new rule; .v3-day-head (heading size + a --gap-50 rung before its rows); .v3-day-summary (cursor + weight on the native <summary>); .v3-day-body (its own em indent, per css skill's 'a control keeps its own em' rule - this is a disclosure body, not a page region or a card). Everything else reuses what already exists: flow/flex/v/gap-25/wrap/muted utility classes, and the 'show more days' button wears the already-declared .v3-count-toggle look (a plain underlined text button) instead of a new class for the same look.

assign.outcome: **A `days` view on `/framework/ai/v/3/` turns roughly 700 scattered task logs into a short, readable report of what actually happened — and it is now the site's front door.** Newest day first, one row per task that landed that day, collapsed to the one-line headline the task wrote for itself at landing (`day.jsonl`); a click reads that task's own `task.jsonl` once for the full outcome, its links, and a link to the task page. Today's still-running tasks show as one quiet `working — <now>` line each, `<now>` read live the same way a running task's own card already does. `days` is the new default view of both `/framework/ai/v/3/` and `/framework/ai/` (which already renders this page) — `now`/`grid`/`timeline` are one click away exactly as before, `?view=` and a saved preference both still work. Proven headless at 400/1280/1920: zero console errors, no horizontal overflow, a fold opens and loads correctly, and today's row count (8) matches `day.jsonl`'s own landed-line count (8) exactly. ![today's report, opened](/framework/ai/2026-09-22/days-view/shots/days-1280.png) [Task page](/framework/ai/2026-09-22/days-view/) - [v/3/page.js](/framework/ai/v/3/page.js) (`days_view()` and its helpers) - [v3.css](/framework/ai/v/3/v3.css) - [v/3/readme.md](/framework/ai/v/3/readme.md). Left as a documented tradeoff, not an oversight: the row's headline comes from `day.jsonl`'s own one-line summary, not `assign.outcome`'s own bold sentence — fetching every landed task's `task.jsonl` up front (the way `ext/AITask/dashboard.js`'s `all_tasks()` already does) was measured and rejected at ~700 requests against 32; opening a row reads the real thing. `tokens` below is null - this session's own transcript file was not summed, honestly, rather than guessed.
